title: River Red Gum: Giant Eucalyptus You Can Visit
meta_description: Seville's tallest tree and the tallest in Valencia province are both Australian river red gums. Three mapped, in three Spanish cities.
intro: Seville and the province of Valencia each have a record holder for height, and both are the same Australian tree, growing thousands of kilometres from where it belongs. Eucalyptus camaldulensis follows the seasonal rivers of inland Australia across almost the whole continent, surviving drought by dropping whole limbs and resprouting from the base, which is a habit that makes municipal arborists nervous. Seville pruned its 50 metre specimen in 2025 specifically to reduce the risk of falling branches, and Valencia's crews need aerial platforms and help from the fire service to reach the top of theirs, 41 metres in a park in Benimamet. Barcelona's grew up inside the walled grounds of a charity house in the Raval, which is the only reason there was open soil for it in the densest neighbourhood in the city.
